correctness.rationale: For ordered odd primes \(p<q<r<s\), normalization forces \(p=3\) because the least possible four-factor Euler product for \(p\ge5\) already exceeds one. Then \(q\ge11\) is excluded by \(4000/3993>1\), leaving \(q=5,7\). The \(q=7\) branch gives \(3(r-8)(s-8)=163\); the \(q=5\) branch gives \((r-16)(s-16)=235\), whose factor pairs leave only \((17,251)\). Direct substitution verifies the survivor.

value.rationale: The source explicitly conjectures infinitely many solutions of the variable-support prime equation.
